package_info.why_malicious: The package is part of a coordinated campaign to distribute malware, spam, and scams via the npm ecosystem. It abuses the package registry to lure users into downloading malicious executables, redirecting to phishing or scam sites, and participating in referral or crypto scams. The package contains no legitimate code or documentation and is designed solely for malicious purposes, including malware delivery, credential theft, and monetization through scams.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package page, the README displays a download link to a third-party site controlled by the attacker, enticing the user to click the link, which initiates a download of a malicious file from an external domain, resulting in the user being exposed to malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The README contains only a download link to an external, non-official site, which is a common tactic for distributing malware through social engineering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should provide code or documentation relevant to the package's purpose, not external download links to suspicious or warez files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to official documentation or project homepages, but not to warez or password-protected executables.
key_indicators: README.md contains only a single external download link
Link points to a non-official, shortener-based domain (urluso.com)
No actual npm code or package functionality present

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: File download page offering: Teletek-Electronics-ECLIPSE-32-Engineer-...onics.zip (password-protected zip containing large .exe)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user clicks the download link in the README, the browser is redirected to a phishing site that presents a download page for a password-protected zip file containing a large, padded malicious executable, resulting in the user downloading malware that is designed to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The site mimics legitimate file download portals but delivers a password-protected archive, a common malware delivery tactic to evade detection by security tools and scanners.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documentation or download sites do not deliver password-protected executables, especially not warez or suspiciously large files from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software is distributed via password-protected archives to protect against tampering, but not in the context of warez or from suspicious domains.
key_indicators: Password-protected zip file offered for download
Executable file is padded to approximately 600MB to evade EDR and antivirus scanning
File hosted on attacker-controlled infrastructure with no legitimate association

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malware drops and executes: Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig, disables firewalls, evades sandbox, steals credentials, mines cryptocurrency.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user executes the malicious .exe extracted from the zip file, the executable performs DLL side-loading, disables security tools, drops additional malware payloads (such as Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig), exfiltrates credentials, and initiates cryptocurrency mining, resulting in system compromise, data theft, and resource abuse.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The executable exhibits multiple advanced malware behaviors, including evasion of security tools, credential theft, and crypto mining, and is associated with known malware families.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should perform actions such as disabling security tools, stealing credentials, or mining cryptocurrency, especially when delivered via a warez lure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None. These behaviors are exclusively associated with malware.
key_indicators: Drops and executes multiple known malware families (Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig)
Performs credential theft and cryptocurrency mining
Employs sandbox evasion and persistence mechanisms

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package page, the README displays a referral link to AliExpress, prompting the user to click the link, which redirects them to an e-commerce site with an affiliate code, resulting in potential financial gain for the attacker if purchases are made.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package is used to drive traffic to e-commerce sites for referral rewards, exploiting the npm ecosystem for affiliate marketing rather than any legitimate package purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should not be used for affiliate marketing, referral scams, or unrelated commercial promotion.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate open-source projects may mention sponsors or partners, but not use packages solely for referral traffic or as the only content.
key_indicators: README.md contains only a referral link
No code or legitimate documentation present

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package page, the README displays a Telegram invite link, prompting the user to join a Telegram channel, which lures users into crypto scam communities, resulting in potential exposure to further scams or fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package is used to lure users into scam communities via Telegram, leveraging npm as a vector for social engineering and fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should not be used to promote unrelated social media or scam channels, especially as the sole content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate projects may link to support or discussion channels, but not as the only content or for the purpose of scams.
key_indicators: README.md contains only a scam-related Telegram invite link
No code or legitimate documentation present
Link points to a Telegram group associated with crypto scams

attack_chain.action: User discovers npm package via search or SEO poisoning.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is lured to click on external links.

attack_chain.action: User clicks on the external link in the README (malware, referral, or scam).
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: User downloads a password-protected zip file containing a malicious executable (malware campaign).
Malicious executable runs, evades detection, disables security tools, drops additional malware, steals credentials, and/or mines cryptocurrency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim data, resources, or profits from referral/scam.

behavioral_signatures: npm packages with README.md containing only external links to warez, phishing, referral, or Telegram sites
Links to non-official, shortener-based domains (e.g., urluso.com) in package documentation
Password-protected zip files containing large, padded executables offered via external download pages
Executables that, when run, disable security tools, drop multiple malware families, steal credentials, or mine cryptocurrency
file_indicators: README.md with only a single external link (download, referral, or Telegram invite)
No package code or only placeholder files in the npm package
Password-protected zip files with large .exe payloads (e.g., ~600MB) downloaded from suspicious domains
network_indicators: AliExpress referral URLs containing ?af= affiliate codes
Telegram invite links (e.g., t.me/+u9dz2n6sGos1ZmEy) in package documentation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Flag npm packages whose README.md files contain only external links, especially to warez, phishing, referral, or Telegram sites. Monitor for packages with no code or only placeholder files. Detect downloads of password-protected zip files from suspicious or shortener-based domains, and large executables with behaviors such as disabling security tools, credential theft, or crypto mining. Correlate network activity to known malicious domains and affiliate/referral patterns.
